newsitem.title: NORWAY: Ice hampers rescue of stranded cruise liner.
newsitem.headline: Ice hampers rescue of stranded cruise liner.

text.p: Efforts to free a cruise liner stranded on rocks and sand off the Arctic island of Spitzbergen were hampered on Tuesday by drifting ice, officials said.

Elisabeth Aarsaether, spokeswoman for the governor's office on Spitzbergen which is coordinating the rescue, said the 9,000 deadweight tonne luxury liner, the Hanseatic, was "completely blocked in by ice".
The ship's 145 passengers and 115 crew remained aboard and in good spirits, she said.

"Either the ice is packing in around the ship or it will drift away, we are not sure yet," Aarsaether told Reuters. "There is no danger to the ship or the passengers. According to the captain the atmosphere on board is calm, they are having a good time."
Coastguards planned to unload at least part of the ship's 480 tonne cargo of heavy fuel oil before attempting to drag her free.

But three rescue vessels involved in the operation were forced to pull out of the area to avoid becoming trapped by the ice themselves, Erling Herstad, duty officer at the Bodoe rescue centre in northern Norway, said.
"The rescue attempt has been stopped due to the ice, but the situation is not regarded as critical," he said, adding that weather conditions in the area were overcast but fine.
The Bahamian-registered Hanseatic ran aground on Sunday in the Hinlopen fjord off Spitzbergen's north coast. It was on its way from Norway to Iceland via the scenic island.
There were no injuries and the liner's owners, Hamburg-based Hapag-Lloyd AG, said an inspection of the hull by divers had found only minor damage.
The Hanseatic also ran aground last August. The same captain hit a sandbank on a voyage in northwest Canada, ending the boat's tour through the Arctic for the 268 people on board.
